searchText: re. shorter slot time, im still of the opinion that we ship what's ready, and shorter slot times isn't ready to take into a delivery pipeline atm so imo its kind of a no brainer (catching up on acdc, this is my 2c) lets get the spec updates, get the discussions happening, and start thinking about what it looks like, but I agree with <@554799849288105986> that the shortest path to deliver both restructuring and shorter times is to do slot times second given the state of play of the respective features. I'm working on the spec update for 7732, Francesco has already done forkchoice I think (haven't had time to actually review). <@520034910149410861> also left a bunch of open questions that are good and we should probably revisit. Anyway at this stage in stuck with a matter of form: both implementations and specs are on top of Electra. Not sure what will be easier, if rebase first and then update or the other. I think I'll do the other order <@592004585506340885> We just had a consensus bug on devnet-1 that is a subtle thing that should be caught in spectests I think, not sure how to generate such a test, having trouble generating the regression in go actually https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/15450 cc <@911437720994324570> Thanks for reporting! Agree we should have tests for checking if lookahead initialization at fork is using correct active validator set. We do have tests for this for the epoch processing but it was missing for fork initialization. Filed this issue for it, will take a stab at it: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/4412 This is not something that is only for this particular feature, we've run Kurtosis runs ad-nauseum now, and a bunch of devnets, and this bug shows that we **never** changed the active validator set at the fork, this is kinda crazy There should be standard fork tests where the active validator set changes at the fork, both by exits and by activations Oh wow. Yeah thanks for reporting <@755590043632140352>. And thanks <@911437720994324570> for working on it. We definitely should add tests for this like you describe. I'm shocked we don't have these, we went through 5 forks already 🙂 devnet 2* <@755590043632140352> <@592004585506340885> I have added spec-tests that checks that proposer lookahead initialization uses the correct active validator set at fork transition. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4413 could we have this for all previous forks too please? this is impossible for previous forks. What needs to be done is to add fork tests (not lookahead tests) for all forks, where there are exits and activations at the fork, and we need to compare the post-state Yes, my tests are just for proposer lookahead initalization at Fulu fork, for the more general variant will need <@592004585506340885> 's assistance 🙏 The way I did it in Go (well, I told Claude to do) is to cook the activation epoch of the validators to be the fork epoch, and that's it

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
re. shorter slot time, im still of the opinion that we ship what's ready, and shorter slot times isn't ready to take into a delivery pipeline atm so imo its kind of a no brainer (catching up on acdc, this is my 2c)
lets get the spec updates, get the discussions happening, and start thinking about what it looks like, but I agree with <@554799849288105986> that the shortest path to deliver both restructuring and shorter times is to do slot times second given the state of play of the respective features.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm working on the spec update for 7732, Francesco has already done forkchoice I think (haven't had time to actually review). <@520034910149410861> also left a bunch of open questions that are good and we should probably revisit. Anyway at this stage in stuck with a matter of form: both implementations and specs are on top of Electra. Not sure what will be easier, if rebase first and then update or the other. I think I'll do the other order

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: <@592004585506340885> We just had a consensus bug on devnet-1 that is a subtle thing that should be caught in spectests I think, not  sure how to generate such a test, having trouble generating the regression in go actually https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/15450

excerpts.author: linoscope
excerpts.content: Thanks for reporting! Agree we should have tests for checking if lookahead initialization at fork is using correct active validator set. We do have tests for this for the epoch processing but it was missing for fork initialization. Filed this issue for it, will take a stab at it: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/4412

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: This is not something that is only for this particular feature, we've run Kurtosis runs ad-nauseum now, and a bunch of devnets, and this bug shows that we **never** changed the active validator set at the fork, this is kinda crazy

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: There should be standard fork tests where the active validator set changes at the fork, both by exits and by activations

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Oh wow. Yeah thanks for reporting <@755590043632140352>. And thanks <@911437720994324570> for working on it. We definitely should add tests for this like you describe.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm shocked we don't have these, we went through 5 forks already 🙂

excerpts.author: linoscope
excerpts.content:
<@755590043632140352> <@592004585506340885> I have added spec-tests that checks that proposer lookahead initialization uses the correct active validator set at fork transition.

https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4413

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: could we have this for all previous forks too please?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: this is impossible for previous forks. What needs to be done is to add fork tests (not lookahead tests) for all forks, where there are exits and activations at the fork, and we need to compare the post-state

excerpts.author: linoscope
excerpts.content: Yes, my tests are just for proposer lookahead initalization at Fulu fork, for the more general variant will need <@592004585506340885> 's assistance 🙏

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: The way I did it in Go (well, I told Claude to do) is to cook the activation epoch of the validators to be the fork epoch, and that's it
